## 2026-10-11 — The admin set `_RELEASE_GATE_URL`, and setting it exposed a defect in my own fix (Q-808)

**Admin, this turn:** `_RELEASE_GATE_URL = https://navbharatai.com/api/release/gate` — **done**, on the Cloud
Build trigger. So Q-141's blocker is cleared and the release gate is now live on the path that ships every
merge. Registered in `docs/claude/ENV_REGISTRY.md` in this same commit, because `cloudbuild.yaml`'s own
default is `''` and a future session reading only the file would conclude the gate is still inert.

### 🔴 The defect the configuration exposed, and it is mine

I was about to verify the wiring by curling the endpoint, and stopped — **because that call would itself have
become the evidence.** Which is the bug:

`/api/release/gate` is **public**; it has to be, because Cloud Build asks it without logging in. The route
recorded a check on **every** GET, and `freezeEnforcementNote` then printed:

> *"A deploy pipeline last asked this gate at … so a freeze does reach the pipeline."*

**A browser, an uptime monitor, a crawler, or me testing the URL wrote that record**, after which the admin
board vouched for a safety control on the strength of it. The store held *that a call happened*; the sentence
stated *who made it*. One fact, two readings, and the stronger one was printed.

🔑 **This is the exact class the module was written to fix** — a status that reports more than its evidence
supports — **shipped inside the fix.** That is why it gets a row (Q-808) and this entry rather than a quiet
patch: the fifth rule's "check whether it has come back before" answers *yes, in my own change*.

**Fix — grade the evidence by what the call actually carried; never infer:**

| what arrived | grade | what the board says |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Release-Gate-Caller: cloudbuild` (the step now sends it) | `pipeline` | *"The deploy pipeline asked this gate at … for commit abc123"* |
| no header, but a real commit SHA | `commit` | *"… very likely the deploy pipeline — but it did not identify itself, so this is not proof"* |
| neither | `none` | **not recorded at all**, so it can never become evidence later |

Locked by `tests/aFreezeThatStopsNothing.test.ts` (31 cases), reversion-proven five ways: record every call
again → 2 fail · print PROVEN without the header → 1 · accept any string as a SHA → 2 · drop the header from
the step → 1 · "tidy" the escaping back to `$URL` → 1.

### ⚠️ And another session fixed a REAL bug in my step — worth more than my own fix

`df7aef5e2`: *"the gate step's bash variables are escaped for Cloud Build — $$URL / $$BODY"*. An unescaped
`$URL` is read by Cloud Build as a **substitution**, and an unknown one fails the build at config parse — so
**my first version of Step 0 would have broken every deploy**, not just the gate. When I shipped it I wrote
that the residual risk was unverifiable from a session (*"no session here can run Cloud Build to prove
otherwise"*). The risk was real and it landed. Two conclusions, both recorded:

1. **A fail-open script is not a safe step if the file it lives in can fail to parse.** My five runtime
   proofs tested the bash; nothing tested that Cloud Build would accept the YAML around it. The safety
   argument covered the wrong layer.
2. The escaping is now **pinned by a test**, so it is never "tidied" back by someone who reads `$$URL` as a
   typo.

**What to watch, since the live effect is only visible on a real deploy:** after the next merge to `main`, the
admin board's Release gate card should change from *"No deploy pipeline has ever asked this endpoint"* to the
proven sentence naming the commit. If it still says *never asked*, the step ran but could not reach the URL —
it fails OPEN, so the deploy still succeeded, and that build's Cloud Build log says which. ⚠️ I cannot check
this myself: outbound to `navbharatai.com` is denied from this session (`connect_rejected`, organization
policy), so this one is the admin's observation to make, not mine to claim.

## 2026-10-11 — Native feel, for the apps NavBharatAI builds AND for NavBharatAI itself

**Admin, verbatim:** *"navbharatai jo app banaye aur navbharatai khud dono ko real netiv app feel aye aisa
banao! aur bhi jyada micro polish karo!!"* — chosen from the three options I had laid out, after they asked
what "native" would actually mean (the answer: today's APK is already a real signed package; what differs is
that a web view sits inside it, so the cheap and visible win is the FEEL, not a Kotlin rewrite).

### Measured first, and the split was lopsided

NavBharatAI's own shell was already well covered: `src/lib/nativeShell.ts` (444 lines — splash, status bar,
haptics with a tap tone and user prefs, back button, keyboard inset), and `index.html` already carried
`viewport-fit=cover` and the Apple meta tags, with a whole "NATIVE-FEEL FIX (admin audit 2026-07-26)" block
in `index.css` for pull-to-refresh, the rubber-band, the tap highlight and text selection.

**The apps it BUILDS had none of it.** `appDefaults.ts` gave a generated app exactly
`width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0` plus a `theme-color`.

🔑 **And the worst gap was structurally invisible to the patcher.** `appDefaults`'s viewport rule is guarded
by `name=["']viewport["']`, and **Vite's own template always ships a viewport** — so the rule never fired and
`viewport-fit=cover` never arrived. Without that one token **`env(safe-area-inset-*)` resolves to 0px on every
device**: a fixed header sits under the notch, a bottom bar under the home indicator, and any safe-area CSS a
generated app writes does nothing at all. **An `ensure`-only patcher cannot fix a wrong ATTRIBUTE on a tag
that is already present** — that is the class, and it is why the viewport is now upgraded in place.

### What shipped

**For generated apps** (`nativeFeel.ts`, wired through `appDefaults.ts`): the viewport upgrade; the
Apple/Android fullscreen meta tags; and a behaviour-only CSS baseline covering the tap flash, the ~300 ms
double-tap delay, pull-to-refresh, iOS's page zoom on a sub-16px input, rotate re-flow, momentum in nested
scrollers, safe-area variables, and a pressed state. Plus a prompt rule for what only the model can decide
per element — `inputMode`/`enterKeyHint` on the right field, 44px targets, safe-area padding on its own bars.

**For our own app** (`index.css`): the audit of what 2026-07-26 left found exactly two gaps, both about the
~100 ms after a finger lands. (1) **A tap was not answered** — removing the tap highlight took away the
browser's crude feedback and put nothing in its place, so a press looked identical to no press until the next
screen arrived. (2) **Hover stuck after a tap**, so a tapped button stayed lit and read as stuck. Momentum was
on the document but not on the IDE's own nested panes.

### Two decisions worth stating, because both could have gone wrong

- 🎨 **The baseline paints nothing.** Every rule is behaviour. A baseline that set a colour would fight every
  generated app's own theme and `THEME_RULES.md`; a test asserts the absence of any hex, `rgb()` or
  `background`/`color` declaration.
- 🔒 **It is a floor, not a ceiling.** Touch rules are scoped to `@media (pointer: coarse)` (a mouse needs
  none of them, and shrinking a button under a click is a web affectation); motion respects
  `prefers-reduced-motion`; selectors name CONTROLS so a paragraph keeps its text selection; and there is no
  universal selector, so a drawing canvas that needs `touch-action: none` still wins.

### ⚠️ Three of my own assertions were wrong on the way, all the same shape

1. I guessed `generateAppDefaults`; the function is **`planAppDefaults`**.
2. I counted `/viewport-fit/` in the output and read **2** as a duplicated tag — the second was the baseline
   CSS's own **comment** explaining why the token matters. The invariant is the META TAG carrying it once, and
   the assertion now says that.
3. **A reversion probe silently tested nothing.** Probe 6 replaced a prompt line that did not exist in that
   exact form, so the file was unchanged and the suite passed — which I read as "the test does not bite"
   until I checked the probe itself. Re-run with the real string, it fails as it should. *A proof that does
   not bite is not a proof — and a probe that does not apply is not a probe.*

### ⚠️ And an existing guard caught my DESIGN, not just my code (same change, 2026-10-11)

The first full gate came back `2 failed`, and one of them was the valuable kind.

**`tests/theBootGuardRanOnOneLaneOfTwo.test.ts` → *"🔴 THE MEASUREMENT FROM THE REPORT: 299 bytes in,
18 KB out"*.** That test caps what WE persist into a user's own `index.html` at **2,000 bytes**, and it
exists because an 18 KB preview shim once got saved into a user's source. My baseline injected ~2.5 KB of
CSS as an inline `<style>` — **exactly the shape it watches for.**

🔑 **The guard was right and my design was wrong.** The baseline is now a FILE (`/nbai-native.css`) plus one
`<link>`, which is the mechanism `appDefaults` already uses for the manifest, the icon and the service
worker. Measured after the change: the generated document grows by **75 bytes**, the CSS is cacheable, and
the user can read, edit or delete one obvious file instead of finding our rules inlined in their page.
Re-proven: putting the inline `<style>` back fails that guard again.

**The second failure was `appDefaults.test.ts > leaves a fully-configured head + registered SW untouched`.**
Its fixture's definition of "fully configured" predated the phone tags — and its head had a viewport with no
`viewport-fit=cover`, which genuinely DOES need something. The invariant it protects (a document needing
nothing is never churned) is unchanged and still asserted; the fixture now includes the new tags, with the
reason written into it.

⚠️ **A third wrong assertion of mine, and the fourth of this change:** I reused the 2,000-byte figure from
that other test in my own case — but it measures a *different* fixture, so the number meant nothing where I
put it, and the case then failed on a `html` variable that was not even in that `describe`'s scope. It now
asserts the thing that actually matters: **our contribution** to the document (<120 bytes), and that none of
the CSS is in the page. *A threshold copied from another test's fixture is not a measurement.*
- **Q-745 (product):** a failed build never reaches the user's GitHub branch.
  - The push is decided by the outcome (`gitPushTarget.ts`).
  - A build that did not work goes to `wip/build-<UTC stamp>`, with a note in the chat.
  - The working branch, the pull request and the merge are left alone.
  - Test: `tests/aFailedBuildNeverReachesTheUsersBranch.test.ts`.
- **Q-781 (product):** a build offers its own preview.
  - The chat engine marks a reply as built when its code lands (`chatBuildMeta.ts`). View Live Preview and the deploy row read that mark.
  - Three dead marker branches are deleted, along with the unanswerable Code Review button.
  - Sibling removed: the deploy panel state, which nothing could ever open.
  - Test: `tests/aBuildOffersItsOwnPreview.test.ts`.
- **Q-248 (honesty):** a size nobody measured is not claimed.
  - The claim audit reads the phone-size check's outcome.
  - "44×44 buttons" or "fits a phone" is corrected out loud as unmeasured or contradicted, unless the check passed.
  - Test: `tests/aSizeNobodyMeasuredIsNotClaimed.test.ts`.
- **Q-123 (iOS):** the iPhone app never teaches a way to pay.
  - On `ios`, `iosPurchaseGuard.ts` removes every buying sentence from the knowledge each AI is handed, and tells the model money cannot be added in this app.
  - The four chat clients send `X-NBAI-Platform`.
  - Test: `tests/theIphoneAppNeverTeachesAWayToPay.test.ts`.

## 2026-10-11 — Round 2 of the native-feel polish: a loading screen has a shape

Stacks on #3669 (the branch, not `main` — `nativeFeel.ts` does not exist on `main` yet, which I found by
branching off `main` and watching the edit fail on a missing file).

### Measured first again, and half of what I was about to propose already existed

| | our own app | a built app |
|---|---|---|
| Screen transition | ✅ `src/lib/screenTransition.ts` — a fade-through, with Material's and iOS's own rationale written down | — |
| Skeleton primitive | ✅ `src/components/ui/Skeleton.tsx` (P-UX.2) | ❌ **nothing** |
| Scroll restoration | ❌ | ❌ |
| Swipe-back | ❌ | ❌ |

So the honest round-2 list was much shorter than the one I announced. **The real gap: the build rule asked
for *"the SHAPE of what is coming"* and handed the model nothing to use.** A rule that names no primitive is
aspirational, not actionable.

**Shipped:** `.nb-skeleton` in the baseline stylesheet — a sized-by-the-app block with a slow opacity pulse,
`pointer-events: none` (decoration must never swallow a tap meant for the content loading underneath), and
no motion under `prefers-reduced-motion`. The build rule now names it with a usable snippet.

### 🎨 The colour decision, and an assertion I had to widen honestly

A skeleton needs a fill, and the baseline's standing promise was that it paints nothing. The fill is
**`currentColor`** — the app's own text colour — so the placeholder is right in light mode, in dark mode,
and in a theme this file has never seen. A hex would have been wrong in at least one of them.

That meant widening my own test. The first version banned any `background:`/`color:` declaration at all;
the real invariant is **"no colour this file CHOSE"**, not "no colour property". The assertion now extracts
every colour value in the stylesheet and requires each to be one of `currentColor`, `transparent` or
`inherit` — which is stricter in the way that matters and permits the one thing that cannot fight a theme.

### ⚠️ A backtick inside a TS template literal, again

The skeleton's CSS comment quoted three identifiers in backticks — and `NATIVE_FEEL_CSS` **is** a template
literal, so each one ended the string. It surfaced as two unrelated-looking `TS1005`s about 170 lines away
from the comment. This repo has recorded the same trap before for the generated journey/explorer modules.
The block now says so in its own text, and a test asserts the CSS contains no backtick.

🔑 **Honest note on that test: the compiler is the real guard, not the assertion.** Reversion probe 4 put a
backtick back and the suite failed at *transform* — the file could not compile, so the assertion never ran.
It earns its place by documenting WHY the rule exists for the next person, not by being the thing that
catches it.

### Scroll: given to the MODEL, deliberately not shipped as a script

Scroll restoration is genuinely missing on both sides, and I did **not** ship a generic implementation for
built apps. A generic restore has to guess the app's routing: in a state-routed SPA the pathname never
changes, so one saved position would be restored onto whatever screen came next — putting the user half-way
down the wrong list. That is trading one problem for another. The router is the one thing the model knows and
this module cannot, so the rule asks for the behaviour (new screen → top; back → the exact position) and
leaves the mechanism to the code that has a router.

⚠️ **And I am not building swipe-back, with the reason rather than silence:** in a tab app "back" is
ambiguous (Home → Studio has no back), Android's hardware back is already handled by
`installBackButtonHandler`, and a swipe-back that guesses wrong subtracts from native feel instead of adding
to it. Recorded as a deliberate non-item, not an omission.

  - Project Mode's size signals moved into APP_SCOPE: a stated scale, a big-software noun with named parts, and a long spec. The thresholds stay in `ProjectPlan.ts`.

Read literally, the decision would have built Blue Berry (144 parts, "resume") and the 6461025c ads platform (429 parts, "Budget") in one pass. A long spec is now vetoed only when the app itself is small.
  - Sibling bug found the same way: the scale reader counted "404 page" as 404 pages, which put a portfolio over Project Mode's 100-page rule. `statedScale` skips an HTTP status before the singular word, and reads no links.
  - Measured on 66,309 test strings at both complexity answers: Project Mode's decision changed for none. APP_SCOPE's line now says LARGE for 14 strings that already went to Project Mode, so the report stops calling them one-shot apps.

- **Q-128 (admin decision 2026-10-11: "one timeline — Time Machine is the one version history; the History tab becomes a view of it"):**
  - One component, `src/components/versions/VersionTimeline.tsx`, is rendered by Time Machine and by the builder's History tab. The session's git steps (preview, compare, rename) stay, folded below the timeline.
  - **Defect found while building it:** Time Machine's Restore only ran `setFiles` and `updatePreview` in the browser. The saved app, which the next build reads, stayed on the newer files, so "Version restored ✓" described one tab's memory. Class: a restore that changes the view, not the thing viewed.
  - Fix: one server route, `POST /api/agentv3/restore-version`, with `versionRestore.ts` doing the planning:
    - it is ownership-checked, and refused while a build runs (this instance, plus the cross-instance lease via `workspaceBuildIsLive`);
    - the app as it stands is saved as a version first ("Before going back to …"); if that copy fails, nothing is changed;
    - the saved file set is replaced, not merged, using GreenGuard's `restorePlan` (no hybrid);
    - the running sandbox is brought to the same state, because the File Guardian only re-adds missing files. If that step fails, the user is told to press Restore again, which is safe to repeat.
  - Siblings fixed in the same change:
    - Time Machine's "current app" was App's legacy `pro-<timestamp>` id, not the builder's sticky v5 session. The builder's workspace is now used, through `historyKeyFor`, which is tested case for case against `restorePointKey`. An app switch now reports itself.
    - "Save this version" saved the screen's copy, which could belong to the app the user had just switched from. It now saves the app's own files server-side (`fromWorkspace`).
    - A version now records which files it could not keep (`omittedPaths`), so a restore never deletes them. For older versions, files are kept and the count is stated.
  - Q-162, decided because `routes/build.ts` was touched: the 410 tombstones `POST /api/build` and `POST /api/build-stream` are deleted. Nothing called them, and their last client was gone before any Play production release.
  - Not a third timeline: `project/VersionStore.ts` is never constructed by live code.
  - Test: `tests/oneVersionTimeline.test.ts`, with four guards reverted and seen to fail. One of those guards first passed when reverted, because no test case put a bad uid's prefix in the workspace id; that case was added.

  - Built: the router's Vertex rung, the vision chain and Doctor AI's Vertex fallback share one client, `lib/vertexGenAI.ts`. It passes an explicit project and region, so the service-account auth is unchanged and an env API key is ignored (checked in the SDK constructor).
  - `@google-cloud/vertexai` is uninstalled with npm; the lockfile only lost packages. Its README said "deprecated as of June 24, 2025 and will be removed on June 24, 2026".
  - The stream forwards `config.abortSignal`, and the 30 s timeout now aborts the request instead of racing a timer.
  - 🔴 **Correction of my own earlier recommendation.** I recommended the swap because it would stop Google billing an abandoned answer. `@google/genai`'s typings say the abort "will not cancel the request in the service. You will still be charged usage". The swap still had to happen, because the old SDK is end-of-life, but its billing benefit was false. The same false claim was corrected in GeminiProvider's comment and in `anAbandonedStreamStopsCosting`'s header. The external limit is now 🟡 Q-819.

The SDK ignored it, so Doctor AI answered on that rung without its own instructions. Fixed; the race call also forwards its signal now. The audit call's unneeded cast was removed too.

  - Test: `tests/oneGoogleSdkForVertex.test.ts`, reverted twice and seen to fail.
- **Q-706 gap (a) — the credential-less build (admin decision 2026-10-11: "this session designs it; the admin verifies it in Cloud Shell on real Cloud Build before it is claimed"):**
  - Built, OFF by default (`NAVBHARAT_APPS_CREDENTIALLESS_BUILD`). With it unset, the job is byte-identical to before; a test pins that.
  - When on, the build has three steps:
    - a privileged step drops build containers' route to the metadata server (`169.254.169.254`) in `DOCKER-USER`, trying both iptables backends, and fails closed if no rule took;
    - `pack build` runs with `--trust-builder=false` and without `--publish`, so the phase that runs the app's scripts never gets the Docker socket;
    - Cloud Build pushes the image (`images:`) after the untrusted step has exited.
  - `buildJobConfig` is the one job builder. `scripts/printCredentiallessBuild.ts` prints it, and `scripts/verifyCredentiallessBuild.sh` submits it in Cloud Shell with the isolation probe and reads `"identity": null` from inside `npm install`.
  - Test: `tests/aBuildRunsUserCodeWithNoCredential.test.ts`, with two guards reverted and seen to fail.
  - Honest state: **🟡 BLOCKED on the admin's Cloud Shell run.** Whether the workers honour the rule is unknowable from here. Gap (b), the egress allow-list, is now Q-820. Hosting stays admin-only until both are closed.
- **Q-796 (admin decision 2026-10-11: "a per-owner view in the admin's app moderation: every app of that person, their states, and one action across them"):**
  - Root cause: a ban was per app, so a person with nine live apps took nine bans, and nothing re-checked a banned person's other live apps.
  - Built:
    - In Admin → Apps, an owner-uid search shows a bar (apps, live) with Unpublish all live and Ban all. It goes through the existing confirmation dialog, with its own sentences (`ownerConfirmCopy`, "at least N" when more pages exist) and the same required reason.
    - Server route `POST /api/admin/owners/:uid/moderate`: per app it runs the single routes' three steps (take offline, which throws unless confirmed; audit line; 180-day record), reports per app, and is bounded with the bound stated.
    - A single Ban returns the person's other live-app count, and the list opens on that person.
  - Design note: the first draft centralised the three steps into one helper. Three existing censuses pin each single route doing them visibly, and that pinning is deliberate. So the single routes are untouched, and a new census pins the owner route's steps and their order to the same ones.
  - Test: `tests/onePersonsAppsOneAction.test.ts`, with two guards reverted and seen to fail. KB entry `admin-built-apps` updated.

## 2026-10-11: Autopsy 46e2d74b — the racing car showed its HEADLIGHTS and LEFT turned it RIGHT (admin: "ek bahut dangerous issue … sab me headlight dikhti hai")

Prompt "Create an racing game for Nokia c 2-01", weak tier (GLM → Kimi). Admin's two bugs, investigated by four parallel
readers + a critic, fixed in three worktree-isolated groups, each adversarially verified, then wired and re-gated here.

- **One defect, not two (measured):** every model faces +Z; the camera ended up on the NOSE side, so the car was filmed
  face-on — and face-on, the driver's left is the screen's right, so correct steering read as mirrored. Kit `update()`
  camera: headlamps 5.56 m vs tail 9.50 m, LEFT → NDC +0.2082; a hand-written +Z car with the usual `car.z + d` camera:
  4.61 m vs 8.30 m, LEFT → +0.70.
- **Why it came back (fifth rule):** the 2026-10-05 fix (e2febbdbd) made the correct camera AVAILABLE (`follow`,
  `driveVehicle`), not the DEFAULT. Three paths missed it: a hand-written game (this build never ran `run_recipe` —
  the prompt named bare `generate_game_*` tools and described kit files as present), the kit's own default (`'chase'`
  unimplemented in `CameraRig.update`; the shell fell back to it), and the kit's own examples (`camera:'thirdPerson'`,
  TS2820, no `ctx.follow`). **Correction (Q-855):** the 10-05 entry above says the `'chase'` kind puts the camera behind
  the car — that was true only of `follow()`, and its premise was never checked against a real build.
  "Speed never increases" is the THIRD recurrence of the 2026-08-25 class, whose guard also lived only in the kit.
- **Fixes:** (A kit) chase implemented, the shell chases the vehicle the PLAYER drives, every recipe example compiled in
  CI, vehicle touch preset, `cameraRelative` and motorcycle signs; (B delivery) the game kit is seeded by the platform
  before the first model call (`gameKitSeed.ts`, kill switch `AGENTV3_GAME_KIT_SEED=off`), every prompt step is
  `run_recipe`, the camera half of the +Z rule in plain three.js, ETA lane decided first; (C checks) review tags read by
  shape, the playtest presses "Start Race" (and gets the explorer's working start label), NOT_RUN is an open warning,
  primed node_modules no longer stale, install-on-import, a write-time note on a hand-written vehicle/camera.
- **Locks:** `theCarIsSeenFromBehind`, `aRecipeExampleCompiles`, `theRacingCarShowedItsHeadlights`,
  `aRacingGameIsStartedAndDriven`, `aReviewTagIsReadByItsShape`, `aPrimedTreeIsNotAStaleTree` — each reverted-and-failed.
- **Queue:** Q-830..Q-865 (36 rows). 🟡 admin decisions: Q-842 (GLM crawl not-a-defect), Q-845 (billing an unplayed
  game), Q-846 (Nokia/keypad device target), Q-860 (flip the default yaw). OPEN follow-ups: Q-843, Q-861..Q-865.

### 2026-10-12 — Q-816: a bot you connected can be disconnected

- **The problem:** Bot Builder could connect a Telegram or WhatsApp bot and offered no way to undo it. `POST /api/bots/disconnect` existed and nothing called it, so it sat in the uncalled-route baseline as "undecided".
- **The class:** a capability the server has and the screen never offers.

  - `GET /api/bots` answered a failed read with an empty list, "you have no bots", while one was live. It now returns 502, and `BotStore.listForUser` returns null.
  - `POST /api/bots/disconnect` answered a failed delete with "not found (or not yours)". It now returns 502, and `remove` returns 'error'. It also checks the bot id shape first.
- **Other changes:** the route left the uncalled-route baseline, and the KB `bot_builder` entry names the new path.

Seven rows built: Q-843, Q-846, Q-861, Q-862, Q-863, Q-864, Q-865. Each is root-caused, its siblings hunted, and locked by a test proven by reversion.

| Row | Problem | Root cause → class | Fix | Lock (reverted ⇒ fails) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q-865 | The accelerator probe could call a working game stalled (a "Get ready" countdown; a slow car under a fixed camera) | One 0.55 s look was taken as proof the car never moves | A second, longer look (2 s, after any countdown); no verdict unless both looks agree | real-Chromium `/race-countdown`, `/race-slow` |
| Q-864 | The kit's chase camera picked a parked car (walk-and-drive) or a rival on the start screen | It guessed "the first vehicle" even where that guess could be wrong | Guess only with one vehicle and no Use button; otherwise follow what the game names | `theCarIsSeenFromBehind` ×3 |
| Q-862 | Install-on-import gave up for the whole build when the install lock was busy | "Busy" was recorded as "done" | Busy is said once, retried silently, capped | `aHandWrittenImportIsInstalled` (the old test encoded the defect) |
| Q-846 | "Nokia C2-01" got a 3D touch game | Nothing read a named device | `deviceTarget.ts`, precision-first; light 2D keys-first build; the user is told plainly | `aPhoneTheAppCannotRunOnIsNamed` |
| Q-843 | "No tests at all" for a game | No recipe shipped a behaviour test. Class: five recipes wrote a vitest test without declaring vitest | The shell ships `controls.test.ts`; every recipe writer declares vitest first | `aGameShipsItsControlsTest` runs it: 5 pass; a mirrored kit gives 2 failed |
| Q-863 | Old and new kit files mixed would not compile (measured: 7 tsc errors) | Nothing could tell an untouched older kit file from someone's edit | `gameKitHistory.ts` (79 versions, from git). An untouched old file is brought up to date; an edited one is kept and named. Sibling: `platformAuthored` | `aKitFileFromAnOlderVersionIsRecognised` (census + tsc), reverted 5 ways |
| Q-861 | Hand-written chase cameras were invisible to the write-time scan | The scan reads code shapes; only playing sees the result | The playtest reads it from pixels: the road moving up means the camera faces the car; LEFT panning left means mirrored steering. Consecutive frames, precision-first | real-Chromium chase / front / mirrored / top-down |

**Two things found on the way, and said plainly:**
- **A read that would have lied.** The first version of the Q-861 probe read a correct top-down road at full speed as "moving backwards" on two frame pairs. The cause was aliasing: lane marks repeat, and the car moved more than half a mark between frames. Only the "three pairs must agree" rule stopped a false verdict, and that is luck, not design. Now any read where more than a quarter of the pairs moved faster than the search can follow gives no verdict at all. A test locks the measured case.
- **Q-845 was built against the admin's decision, and then dropped before it was pushed.** I took "sabhi ke liye han hai" as option (b), which waives the markup for a game that was never played. Then PR #3679 recorded the admin's specific answer on Q-845: *"game chal raha hai. makeup lena chahiye"*. That decision wins. The commit was removed from this branch, and no billing code changed. #3679 closes Q-842, Q-845 and Q-860.

**Watch on the next real racing build:**
- The playtest line should show no camera or steering verdict on a game the kit built.
- A "KIT FILES BROUGHT UP TO DATE" note should appear only when an older game is edited.

### 2026-10-12 — Q-869: the playtest's verdicts no longer depend on frame timing

Another session, gating #3679, reported that under CPU load the full suite flipped two #3678 racing verdicts. Q-865 called a working countdown game stalled. Q-861 missed mirrored steering. The code is mine (#3678), so the row is mine.

**What I could and could not reproduce.**
- I could not reproduce the exact 4-CPU flip.
  - Throttling the page's CPU 4× and 8× did not do it.
  - Three full colour-on suite runs here stayed green.
- What I did reproduce shows the same class. A WORKING racer with a 9 s "Get ready" countdown was called stalled, because the second accelerator look lasted only 2 s.
- The class is a verdict read from frame timing. Q-869 names the same class, and it was a real precision hole even on an idle machine.

**The fix, in two parts.**
- **Part A.** The second look now holds the gas and looks once a second for up to 8 s, stopping as soon as anything moves.
  - "The car never moves" needs the full look, with at least 40 frames drawn. A page that a loaded machine stopped drawing shows the same picture whatever the car does.
  - Flow reads now collect 14 drawn frames, with up to 3 s to draw them.
- **Part B (DNA level, the suggestion in Q-869).** For three.js games, the camera and steering verdicts are read from the SCENE, not from pixels.
  - three.js announces its renderer to `__THREE_DEVTOOLS__`. Wrapping `render()` gives us the scene and the camera.
  - Positions are state, so a slow machine moves them less, never the wrong way.
  - The vehicle is the object the accelerator sped up over its idle speed, so a traffic car is never chosen.
  - The scene only judges when the camera follows the vehicle. A treadmill world otherwise reads as "camera ahead" — measured, ahead = 1.
  - Pixels judge only what the scene cannot, and never against it.

**Locks.**
- Real Chromium and real three.js: chase, front, mirrored and treadmill pages, each with a faster traffic car. Margins: ahead ±1, looks 1, turn ±33–38°.
- The 9 s countdown and lost-first-key pages.
- Reverted 5 ways: the long look, the frame guard, the follow guard, the idle subtraction, and the scene's precedence.
- The KB was updated: the camera check reads a 3D game's scene, and a busy machine is never read as a stalled car.

## 2026-10-12 — AUTOPSY `50378049`, Q-905: a module was "done" because its TURN succeeded, not because it delivered its files

Second PR from the BlockWorld autopsy (the first, #3684, fixed Q-900…Q-904 — a plan-time prediction
outranking a live app).

**The defect.** The plan's module 1 was *"Shared Types & Constants"*, owning `src/types/index.ts` and
`src/constants/index.ts` and carrying the frozen contract every later module would import. The builder
ignored the scope, wrote the whole game — 56 files — and **never those two**. The route settled it with
`result.ok ? markModuleStatus(…, 'done')` (`agentv3.ts:25137`): *"the turn succeeded"* taken as *"this
module delivered its files"*. The user read `✅ Module … done — 1/15`.

**The damage is downstream and certain.** `moduleBuildContext` hands every DONE module's contract to the
next turn under the heading *"ALREADY-BUILT MODULES — their files exist in the workspace. Import from
them using ONLY these frozen contracts"*. Module 2 would be told, in writing, to import exact names from
a file that does not exist. The model cannot win that turn.

⚠️ **It is the unhunted half of autopsy `8e124182`.** That autopsy is the mirror image — *"module 1's
turn wrote 33 files, the whole app, and the plan still recorded 1 of 14 done"* — and its fix,
`reconcilePlanWithWrites`, promotes OTHER modules whose planned paths were all written. It is path-exact
by design ("precision over recall"), so a builder that invents its own structure matches nothing. One
half of the reconciliation shipped; this is the half that asks whether the module in progress delivered
its own share.

**The fix.**
- `undeliveredOwnFiles(mod, present)` — pure; which of a module's own files the PROJECT still lacks.
  Asked against `actuator.listFiles`, never the turn's write set: a file an earlier turn wrote is
  delivered, and asking only about this turn would call it missing.
- `recordModuleDelivery(plan, id, present)` — records it on the module (`undelivered?: string[]`), so
  the fact is durable across turns; module 2's turn is a different request.
- `contractIsUnbacked(mod)` — true only when the module owns files and EVERY one is missing. A
  partially delivered module keeps its contract: the names it did write are real.
- `moduleBuildContext` withholds an unbacked contract and tells the turn why, instead of handing it
  names under a false heading. A partial delivery hands the contract forward with the missing file named.
- `PROJECT_MODULE_FILES_UNDELIVERED` — an `info` measurement of OUR process, registered in both
  `BuildDiagnostics.ts` and `buildFindingSuggestions.ts` so it can never become a finding against the
  user's app. The user's line is honest too: not a flat "done", but *"this step built the app its own way
  rather than those exact files"*.

🔒 **The status is deliberately NOT `failed`.** On the reported build the user got a complete, running
game; *"module 1 failed"* would be its own lie. The status is left alone — what changes is that the plan
RECORDS what is missing and never passes a contract nothing backs.

**Additive by construction:** a plan nobody measured keeps `undelivered` absent, and `contractIsUnbacked`
is false for an absent record, so behaviour is byte-identical to today. A `listFiles` that fails leaves
the plan exactly as it is now (*"unasked is not undelivered"*).

**Locked by** `tests/aPlanThatBecameFiction.test.ts` — 19 cases on the reported plan's real shape.
**Reversion-proven twice:** stop withholding the unbacked contract → 1 fail; ask the turn's writes
instead of the project → 1 fail. A case also asserts the pre-fix state still hands the fictional contract
forward, so the reversion lives in the suite rather than in a shell history.

**Still OPEN from the same root (rowed, not forgotten):** the plan's remaining 14 modules are still
queued and billable on a build whose app already exists. That is `8e124182`'s original damage and it
needs a decision about money and the plan's lifecycle, so it is not taken silently here.
## 2026-10-12 — AUTOPSY `50378049` (BlockWorld, a voxel game): a plan-time PREDICTION outranked an OBSERVED fact, and six verdicts lied at once

**The report.** Weak tier, free, ~20.7 min, `ok: true`, 368 items, 0 errors, 5 warnings, 1 unresolved,
`RELEASE_GATE: UNKNOWN`, billed ₹129.6 / $1.3366.

**The contradiction, in the report's own words.** The timeline carried `PREVIEW_PUBLISHED` — *"Preview
address is live at https://5173-i6p2mx9hgq3xqukkl2q3o.e2b.app"* — and `RUNTIME_VERIFIED` — *"the app ran
in the browser with no actionable console errors"*. In the same report: `RELEASE_GATE: UNKNOWN` (*"no live
preview was ever available, so nothing here was proven to RUN"*), `E2E_SCAFFOLD_SKIPPED`,
`LAST_CHANCE_PROOF_SKIPPED` (*"No preview URL was ever available"*), `MARKUP_WAIVED_NO_PREVIEW` ($1.3366
instead of $5.0098) — and the user was told, about a running game, **"There is nothing to open yet"**.

**Root cause, traced in code, not guessed.** Project Mode's module 1 was *"Shared Types & Constants"*,
which does not own the app's entry, so `shellModuleFor` predicted a later module would assemble the app
(`moduleAwaitsShell`), and the module prompt told the builder *"do NOT start or publish a preview this
turn"*. The builder ignored the scope and wrote the WHOLE GAME — 56 files — and published a real address.
`routes/agentv3.ts`'s preview subscriber read `type === 'preview' && !moduleAwaitsShell`, so it
**discarded the address**, and every proof in the engine is gated on `lastPreviewUrl`. One prediction
disarmed six verdicts.

**A SECOND, independent root cause on the same sentence.** `gateEvidence.previewUrlPublished =
Boolean(lastPreviewUrl)` wrote an explicit `false`, and `fillGateFromLedger` fills a field only when it
is `undefined` — so the evidence ledger's own `PREVIEW_PUBLISHED` record could never correct it. Either
cause alone reproduces the report.

🔴 **SECOND APPEARANCE — the earlier fix was incomplete, and saying so is the point.** `releaseGate.ts`'s
`previewUrlPublished` field exists for this exact false sentence, from the Fight 3D report (`5e2de8c4`,
2026-08-27). That fix corrected the READER and left the SOURCE suppressible. Seven weeks later the class
came back through a route nobody had hunted.

**The fix (the direction of authority, not a new check).** An OBSERVATION outranks a PREDICTION:
- `ProjectPlan.shellStillAwaited(awaitsShell, previewUrl)` — pure; null the moment an address is up.
- The subscriber keeps the address whatever the plan predicted; `awaitsShellNow()` is the one question
  every reader asks (the recap, the markup notice, the runtime record, the gate's excuse, the
  `RELEASE_GATE` severity, the unproven measurement, the mobile + playtest proofs, the review deferral).
- The gate asserts only the POSITIVE for `previewUrlPublished`, so the ledger can still answer.
- `shouldAttemptPlatformPreview` deliberately keeps the RAW prediction: it decides whether to CREATE a
  preview the module was told not to publish, which is not the honesty fix.

**Why it cannot break autopsy `6a5fb04b`, which the prediction exists for:** a module turn that really
has nothing openable publishes no address, so the prediction is returned unchanged and behaviour is
identical. The only turns that change are the ones that published a live address — the lying case. The
starter-page protection is `ToolDispatcher.setStarterExpected`, a separate mechanism, and
`_blockIfStillTheStarterApp` re-checks the entry itself (verified, not assumed).

**Locked by** `tests/aPredictionOutrankedTheApp.test.ts` — the truth table, a CENSUS pinning the raw
variable at 4 code sites so a new reader fails the build, the subscriber's condition, the positive-only
assertion, the end-to-end ledger→gate read on the report's real codes, and a REVERSION case that asserts
the old explicit `false` still prints the false sentence. Reverted both bugs: 3 of 13 failed.

**Ledger: 15 items, Q-900…Q-914.** ✅ 5 resolved here (Q-900 the root, Q-901 the gate's false sentence,
Q-902 "nothing to open yet", Q-903 the two skipped proofs, Q-904 the waived margin). 🔸 10 OPEN and rowed
in `BUILD_REPORT_QUEUE.md`: Q-905 a module marked `done` having delivered none of its own files · Q-906
`READY_BEFORE_END` then 62 more steps over 1019 s · Q-907 a `[BUILD CHECKPOINT]` the model had to disobey
twice · Q-908 24 abandoned recipe files with the orphan hand-back disabled by `starterExpected` · Q-909
the recipe shell's API guessed wrong six times · Q-910 9 TypeScript writes skipped after a `package.json`
change · Q-911 a recipe shipped a test whose runner was not installed · Q-912 three no-progress nudges and
a `console_errors` LOOP GUARD · Q-913 the dark screen rationalised rather than verified · Q-914
`DESIGN_CONSISTENCY` 60/100 shipped (45 hardcoded colours).

**Honest limit of this entry:** one item from the first pass — an `edit_file` ambiguous-match failure —
could not be re-verified against the report text and is therefore NOT counted. It is not in the ledger
rather than in it unproven.

## 2026-10-12 — AUTOPSY `50378049`, Q-911: we shipped a test into the user's app and told them to run a command their app did not have

Third PR from the BlockWorld autopsy (#3684 → Q-900…Q-904; #3686 → Q-905).

**The defect, and it is a second-absolute-rule one.** Every 3D game NavBharatAI builds ships
`src/game/controls.test.ts`, and that file — in the USER's own project — said *"Your test runner runs it
(npm test, or vitest run)"*. The default Vite scaffold's `package.json`
(`ViteReactProviderContents.ts`) defines exactly three scripts: `dev`, `build`, `preview`. **There is no
`test` script.** So `npm test` in that app answers `npm error Missing script: "test"`. We wrote the
test, we wrote the instruction, and the instruction did not work. `AppKnowledgeBase` repeated the claim
to every AI in the product: *"…that the project's own test command runs"*.

**Root cause: the script-writing lived in a CALLER instead of in the shared helper.** `withVitestDeclared`
declared the dependency and stopped there — and `declared` is not `runnable`. Two of the three paths that
ship a test had worked around that in their own code (`projectKit.ts` added `test: 'vitest run'` with its
own copy of the string; `e2eScaffold.ts` adds `test:e2e` before telling anyone to run it). The game kit,
which reaches the helper through `run_recipe → writeRecipeFiles → declareVitestForRecipeTests`, had no
such copy — so it was the one path that shipped the instruction without the script. Q-843 built the
dependency half three days ago and this was the half its sibling hunt did not reach.

**The fix (the class, not the instance).**
- `withVitestDeclared` now ensures BOTH: the devDependency and a real `test` script. Its condition
  changed from *"is vitest declared?"* to *"can the shipped test be run?"*, so a project that already
  declares vitest but has no script is no longer skipped.
- `PLATFORM_TEST_SCRIPT` is exported once — the string two places wrote and a third was missing.
- `projectKit.ts`'s private copy is deleted; it is now one call, so no future caller can forget.
- An author's own `test` script is never overwritten. The npm-init placeholder (`no test specified`) is,
  because `testRunner` already refuses to treat it as a suite.
- The shipped test's own comment and the KB sentence now name a command that works, and the KB records
  what was false before it (the system's honesty, fifth step of the fourth rule).

🔒 **WHY ADDING THE SCRIPT CANNOT BRING BACK A KNOWN FAILURE — checked, not assumed.**
`testRunner.detectTestPlan` prefers a project's own `test` script, so apps now take that branch instead
of the inferred-vitest one. A bare script there would have lost the `--exclude 'e2e/**'` that stops
vitest collecting our unrun Playwright starter — the 2026-08-25 false `vitest: FAIL` that the release
gate escalated to "Not shippable" for a game the admin was playing. **Autopsy `9cca1fd5` (2026-09-17)
already closed that hole on the script branch**, forwarding the same exclusion through the package
manager's `--` passthrough. A case in the new test pins that guard, because this fix's safety rests on it,
and a note in `testRunner.ts` records the check so nobody re-derives the worry.

**Locked by** `tests/aShippedTestCanActuallyBeRun.test.ts` — 11 cases, including a CENSUS of the paths
that ship a vitest test, the real Vite scaffold's actual script list as the premise, and the 9cca1fd5
guard. `theEventBookingAutopsy.test.ts`'s *"nothing is written when it is already declared"* case was
**widened, not weakened**: declared AND runnable is now the condition for doing nothing, with the reason
recorded in place. **Reversion-proven three ways:** stop adding the script → 8 fails · go back to
"declared is enough" → 2 · restore `projectKit`'s private copy → 1.

⚠️ **I hit the backtick-inside-a-template-literal trap TWICE in this one change** — in
`GAME_CONTROLS_TEST` and again in the `AppKnowledgeBase` string — the same trap #3671 recorded. Both
surfaced as parse errors away from the edit (`TS1128` at `AppKnowledgeBase.ts:3785`, and an oxc parse
error that made the test file report "no tests"). Fixed with quotes, and the note is in the test file
rather than in a session's memory.

## 2026-10-12 — AUTOPSY `50378049`, Q-906 **and** Q-907: one root cause, two report lines — the engine told a module turn its app was finished at step 10

Fourth PR from the BlockWorld autopsy (#3684 → Q-900…Q-904 · #3686 → Q-905 · #3688 → Q-911).

**The two report lines turned out to be the same mistake.** `READY_BEFORE_END` said the app was judged
finished at step 10 (100/100) and the build then ran **62 more steps over 1019 s**; separately, a
`[BUILD CHECKPOINT]` told the model to STOP after one file and the model **correctly overrode it twice**.
Tracing the checkpoint's text found it: that message IS `doneSignal.doneSteer`, injected because
`appIsDone` scored the project 100/100 at the first check (`minStep` 8, `everyN` 10 → step 10).

**Why the score was 100 on an app that did not exist yet.** The build was a Project Mode module turn
(module 1, *"Shared Types & Constants"*) AND the game kit had seeded a complete, working 3D game shell
before the model's first call (`GAME_KIT_SEEDED`). `assessBuildReadiness` measures the PROJECT, so it
scored **our own seed**, said "complete and healthy", and the engine told the model:

>     [BUILD CHECKPOINT] … the app is complete and healthy — 100/100, no blockers.
>     If everything the user asked for is present, STOP HERE: write your summary and hand the app over.

🔴 **Had the model obeyed, the user would have been handed NavBharatAI's own seeded shell as their voxel
game.** The 62 "overrun" steps were not an overrun at all — they were the user's game being built.

**It is the THIRD time this reasoning has been accepted in `doneSignal.ts`, and the first two never hunted
this sibling.** `wroteThisRun` (autopsy 1389f0d5) and `editingExistingApp` (autopsy 2b1f845e) are the same
thought; 2b1f845e states it in full: *"The score measures the PROJECT's health; on an edit the project was
healthy before the turn began, so the score cannot say whether the REQUEST is done."* And
`readyOverrunNote` ALREADY carried the module case in its own words — *"this turn built one project module
… not the whole app, so the project score cannot say when it was done"*. **The sentence was written; the
guard never reached `shouldCheckDone`.** The explanation and the behaviour disagreed, and the explanation
was right.

**The fix.** `shouldCheckDone` and `endOfTurnReadyMark` both take `projectModule` and stand down for a
module turn. `AgentRunner` passes it as a **getter** (`projectModule?: () => string | null`) for the same
reason `hasExistingFiles` is one: the route chooses the module long after `baseRunnerOpts` is built, so a
value would always be null.

🔑 **Both guards were required, not just the steer.** `readyOverrunNote`'s honest *"Not measured: this turn
built one project module"* line fires only when there is NO mark — so a mark recorded by the end-of-turn
gate made that sentence **unreachable** for every module turn it judged, and the admin instead read a
62-step overrun of a finished app. A test asserts both directions.

**Locked by** `tests/aModuleIsNotAnAppToBeDoneWith.test.ts` — 11 cases on the reported build's own numbers,
including that the steer is unchanged for the builds it is for, and the wiring census (both
`shouldCheckDone` call sites plus the mark). **Reversion-proven three ways:** drop the steer carve-out → 1
fail · drop the mark carve-out → 2 · pass the route's value instead of a getter → 1.

**🔸 THE OPEN HALF, recorded rather than guessed.** The same collision can happen on a NON-module build: the
game kit seeds a working app, the model writes a few files, and the done check scores OUR seed 100/100. The
module carve-out does not cover that, and the honest fix needs a measured threshold for "enough of the
BUILDER's own work to judge" (`gameKitSeed.builderWrittenCount` is the input). Inventing that number from
one report is exactly what the fourth rule forbids, and this module's own discipline is measure-first — so
it is an OPEN root cause awaiting a report where a seeded, non-module build gets the checkpoint early. It
becomes a `BUILD_REPORT_QUEUE.md` row when #3684 (which holds this autopsy's rows) merges.

**One existing guard was RE-ANCHORED, not weakened** (`theCommitMessageWasNotADevServer.test.ts`). It
counted the literal `editingExistingApp: … === true })` — the flag followed immediately by the closing
brace — so it was really asserting that the flag is the LAST property in the call, and adding a property
after it broke the guard without touching anything it protects. It now asserts the intent directly (every
`shouldCheckDone` call contains the flag), which a reordering cannot break and a removal still can —
proven by dropping the flag from one call and watching it fail.

⚠️ **A PROCESS SLIP WORTH RECORDING, because the gate is what caught it.** After moving this work onto its
own branch I ran a reversion probe without re-staging, so `git checkout -- AgentRunner.ts` restored that
file to HEAD and **silently discarded the whole runner half of the fix**. `typecheck` and the targeted
tests had already passed — on the tree *before* the probes — and the first full-suite run on the branch
then failed on exactly one case: the wiring census. Two of safeguard #5's rules did their job together:
*stage before you probe*, and *run the gate LAST, on the final state*. The census existed because a
reader of this fact could be forgotten; it caught the fix itself going missing.
